title: Equality structure of the LP2-53 red passage
question: Does the 51-rune red passage on LP2-53 have the equality structure of archived decoded GP passages, and does it differ from the same page’s black text?
reader_question: Is the red passage statistically different from the rest of its page?
summary: The 51 red runes are flatter than every matched decoded-reading window but fall within the same-page black-text range.
finding: Red IoC is 0.0298 with 26 distinct runes; 2,492 archived solved-reading windows have minimum IoC 0.0400 and at most 23 unique runes. Red IoC lies within 78 black-text window values on LP2-53. Its zero adjacent repeats also occur in 21.55% of 10,000 red-rune shuffles.
limitations: The windows overlap and describe this fixed corpus, not independent probability trials. Equality statistics are necessary constraints under bijective substitution, not a decryption or proof that red and black use the same cipher.
next_steps: A specific red-passage cipher proposal must preserve or predict the measured equality structure and produce a held-out continuation beyond a chosen phrase.

scope.representation: Original LP2-53 image and pinned transcription; red rune ordinals 128–178 inclusive (last rune of line 6 plus all of lines 7–9), excluding punctuation/artwork. Eight archived decoded GP output-index sections, omitting LP2-56 hash target.
scope.procedure: Compute 51-rune red IoC, adjacent equal pairs and unique count; compare with all length-51 windows in eight solved GP sections and 78 same-page black-prefix windows; shuffle the red indices 10,000 times for the adjacent-repeat order control.
scope.parameters: 51 red runes, 2,492 overlapping solved-section windows, 78 overlapping black-page windows, 10,000 seeded red shuffles.
scope.exclusions: Key or crib searches, alternative span boundaries, literal English-letter controls, LP2-56 hash target, external corpora and any inference of a solved message.

review.reviewer: Independent page-text and decoded-trace checker with planted rune permutation and red-shuffle replay

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; preserve original manuscript image and archived known-reading trace bytes.
